_readme: Grounded facts the AI features may use for FMNH PM9476. Every fact names its source. The AI is told to use these and nothing else, so add per-bone facts under `structures` only from the paper or the Dryad README, never from memory. Bone name, side and source file are added automatically from the manifest.

specimen.text: Palaeolagus haydeni is an early lagomorph important for reconstructing whether the last common ancestor of crown lagomorphs was more leporid-like or more ochotonid-like.
This study presents comprehensive CT-based cranial anatomy of Palaeolagus haydeni, the type species of the genus; the mixed cranial architecture supports its status as a stem lagomorph.
FMNH PM9476 is an almost complete cranium with mandible in occlusion from the early Oligocene Brule Formation of Nebraska, USA.
specimen.source: Wolniewicz & Fostowicz-Frelik 2021, Front. Ecol. Evol. / Dryad methods

specimen.text: In this specimen the skull roof is partially missing (posterior frontals and parietals lost during sedimentation); the anterior nasals and the left zygomatic arch are also largely damaged.
Of characters scored against crown lagomorphs, Palaeolagus showed many leporid-like and ochotonid-like states plus several unlike either crown group, consistent with a stem position.
The Dryad deposit provides PLY segmentations of individual cranial elements and complexes from the μCT scan of FMNH PM9476.

maxilla_teeth_and_jugal_complex_l.text: The paired maxillae form the posterolateral rostrum and central palate, bear all cheek teeth, and contribute to the anterior orbital margin; both maxillae are well preserved except the anterior left maxillary corpus, which is extensively damaged.
Only a small portion of the left zygomatic (jugal), adjacent to the zygomatic process of the maxilla, is preserved in FMNH PM9476.

maxilla_teeth_and_jugal_complex_r.text: The maxillary corpus produces two anterior prongs that insert into facets on the premaxilla; the alveolar process bears six alveoli (P2–4 and M1–3), with M1 the largest.

The right zygomatic is almost completely preserved (posterior tip excepted) and is tightly co-ossified with the maxillary zygomatic process; its lateral zygomatic fossa was an attachment for the lateral masseter.
The lateral wall of the maxillary corpus is perforated by a lacework of small openings like extant leporids, rather than a single large facial fenestra as in ochotonids.

premaxilla_and_incisor_l.text: The paired premaxillae form the anterolateral rostrum, contribute to the anterior palate, and carry both pairs of upper incisors.
The left premaxilla in FMNH PM9476 is extensively damaged anteriorly relative to the better-preserved right side.

premaxilla_r.text: The right premaxilla is well preserved except for slight abrasion of its anterior surface; the alveolus for the anterior upper incisor (dI2) is larger and more anterodorsal than that for the posterior upper incisor (I3).
Both upper-incisor alveoli curve dorsally through the premaxillary corpus; the dI2 alveolus continues into the maxilla, whereas the I3 alveolus is contained within the premaxilla.

mandible_and_dentition_l.text: The mandible is well preserved except for the posterior portions of both mandibular rami and the right coronoid process, which are broken.
Each hemimandible has two mental foramina—an anterior one along the diastema and a posterior one below p3—a combination unlike either crown leporids or ochotonids alone.

mandible_and_dentition_r.text: Alveoli for di2 and for p3–p4 and m1–m3 are present; the m3 alveolus is markedly smaller than the other cheek-tooth alveoli.
The lateral mandibular ramus forms an extensive masseteric fossa; medially, a pterygoid fovea and pterygoid fossa mark attachments for the lateral and medial pterygoid muscles.

nasal_l.text: The paired nasals form the dorsal rostrum and roof of the nasal cavity; in FMNH PM9476 only the posterior parts are preserved, the anterior portions being abraded.
The nasal widens posteriorly to a frontal process with a V-shaped suture against the frontal—more like extant leporids than Ochotona, whose nasals do not broaden in the same way.

nasal_r.text: Ventrally each nasal bears a longitudinal nasoturbinate (ethmoidal) crest separating the dorsal nasal meatus from the roof of a relatively shallow ethmoidal fossa.

frontal_fp_l.text: Both frontals are well preserved anteriorly, but the supraorbital processes and posterior frontal squamae are missing in FMNH PM9476.
The frontal squama has an approximately flat dorsal surface resembling ochotonids more than the strongly arched leporid braincase roof; ventral fossae mark the olfactory bulbs.

frontal_fp_r.text: Anteromedially the frontal forms a triangular nasal process; anterolaterally a maxillary process separates the nasal process of the premaxilla from the maxilla in dorsal view.

palatine.text: The palatine is a single unpaired element forming the posterior hard palate; in FMNH PM9476 it is completely preserved.

Each hemipalatine has a horizontal lamina with a major palatine foramen enclosed within the palatine, plus accessory palatine foramina—more leporid-like than the multiple small openings of ochotonids.

lacrimal_r.text: Only the right lacrimal is partially preserved; its orbital plate and facial process are largely abraded, but the lacrimal hamulus is well preserved.
The hamulus forms the medial wall of the posterior nasolacrimal canal and bears a lacrimal crest along its length.

frontal_presphenoid_basisphenoid_squamos.text: In the CT segmentation, the orbital portion of the frontal, presphenoid, basisphenoid, and squamosal are figured as a complex because internal sutures are not visible in the CT data.
The basisphenoid, alisphenoids, and pterygoids are well preserved in FMNH PM9476 because limited external preparation left the cranial base intact—unlike most other P. haydeni skulls.

tympanic_l.text: The ectotympanic forms a greatly expanded tympanic bulla; laterally it bears an osseous external acoustic meatus directed posterolaterally, resembling leporids rather than the short lateral meatus of ochotonids.

tympanic_r.text: Posterior to the external acoustic meatus, the dorsal ectotympanic surface forms a fissure for the mastoid process; anteromedially a styliform process underlaps the basisphenoid.

mastoid_l.text: The lateral mastoid exposure in Palaeolagus haydeni is more extensive than in leporids and has a smooth surface shared with ochotonids, rather than the extensively pitted mastoid of leporids.

mastoid_r.text: The mastoid exposure forms a prominent mastoid (paroccipital) process that inserts into a fissure on the dorsal surface of the ectotympanic; the authors describe the petrosal mastoid exposure as more ochotonid-like than leporid-like overall.

basioccipital_interparietal_complex.text: The basioccipital is mediolaterally narrowest anteriorly and widens toward the foramen magnum—ochotonid-like rather than the anteriorly broad basioccipital of leporids.
Ventrolateral crests (tympanic processes) of the basioccipital overlap the medial walls of the tympanic bullae, another ochotonid-like basicranial feature highlighted in the discussion.
